    THE SCIENCE BEHIND THE ADVENTURE

    Real data. Clear assumptions.

    Know what comes from NASA, what the game calculates, and what belongs to our fictional expedition.

    Mission assumptions & limitations

      ASTRA uses contextual rules grounded in the mission state. The ten lessons, equipment targets and power budgets are authored learning exercises. Greenhouse demand is a simplified power allocation, not a crop-growth simulation. The shelter and airlock drills model training procedures. Solar output and radio quality are game models; collected rocks and supply crates are fictional. Multiplayer is not included.

      Independent educational prototype · no NASA endorsement implied
      YOUR FIELD GUIDE

      A small step to get started.

      Start at level 1. Read the Next action card, follow the gold objective marker, and use its action button when you arrive. Completing the practical task earns your badge and unlocks the next level immediately. Ten lessons take you from Junior Cadet to Qualified Junior Astronaut. Knowledge checks earn optional bonus XP.

      W A S DMove across the surface
      CLICK / TAPPlot a route without dragging

      MSwitch surface / orbital data
      PPause or resume the expedition
      The white ribbon is your return route. The orange marker is your next objective. Optional cyan surveys earn research points. Tap the ASTRA button to open your companion. Drag either panel by its header to move it; focus the handle and use arrow keys for keyboard movement. ↺ resets a panel’s position.
      Drag with the mouse or one finger to look through 360°. Drag vertically or use ↑ ↓ to change elevation. Pan terrain switches dragging to move the camera across the ground; Shift-drag or middle-drag also pans. Show objective frames your current destination; Overview shows YOU and the destination together. Astronaut view (F) places the camera at your visor, and Show objective turns your helmet toward the marker. WASD follows where you look. Follow astronaut restores your moving camera. The [ ] keys turn and , . change elevation. Equipment controls stay beside the 3D scene: watch the instructor, then perform each action yourself.
      Surface is the playable world. Orbital data is an observation view; use Return to play to get back. The tracker always marks YOU. Go to objective calculates a terrain route; WASD takes over. Restore a hidden tutorial from Settings or the Tutorial button. Your badges and unlocked levels are saved in this browser.
      GAME SETTINGS

      Make the mission yours.

      The opening plays once when you enter the game, then continues into your training. This setting applies on your next visit; Skip story skips only the current opening.

      Action-by-action guidance is enabled.

      Music, motion, labels, tutorial preference, badges and unlocked levels are remembered in this browser when storage is available. Showing the tutorial keeps your current progress.
      JUNIOR ASTRONAUT ACADEMY

      Your path to the crew.

      Ten practical missions. Complete each field task to earn a badge and unlock the next mission. Knowledge checks are optional. Selecting a level begins that lesson from its briefing.
